name: nav-buttons-hug-the-right-edge
description: back/forward/reload stay flush with .sbnav's own right edge, at whatever width the sidebar is currently docked at. .sbnav now spans left:clearance to right:10px instead of shrinking to its content, and .sbback carries the lab's first class (margin-left: auto, swipe-lab.html:58) so the group is pushed against that edge rather than sitting packed next to the traffic lights. The reading is relative - the group's right edge against the row's own right edge, not an absolute pixel - so it holds at any width the resize below lands on, the same reasoning a-resize-carries-the-sidebar-contents-with-it uses for the pane. The reload click below is a REAL OS click (cgevent) at the button's on-screen position, which crosses AtriumClientView::NonClientHitTest before it ever reaches the DOM - a DOM-dispatched click would bypass that native carve entirely and prove nothing about it.

actions.note: first paint, and the nav row announces itself

actions.expression: (() => { const row = document.querySelector('.sbnav'); if (!row) { return 'no row'; } return [...row.children].map((b) => b.className.split(' ').filter((c) => c !== 'navdim').join(' ')).join('|'); })()
actions.note: order and the first class do not move with a resize, so this is checked once. navdim (back/forward greyed out with nowhere to go) is stripped before comparing - a structural check on order and base classes, not on the transient nav-ability state a fresh fixture happens to start in

actions.expression: (() => { const row = document.querySelector('.sbnav'); const reload = row && row.querySelector('.sbreload'); if (!row || !reload) { return 'no row'; } const pad = parseFloat(getComputedStyle(row).paddingRight) || 0; return Math.round(row.getBoundingClientRect().right - pad - reload.getBoundingClientRect().right); })()

THE MEASUREMENT: reload's centre at the dragged-to width 340. x = 340 - kNavGroupRightInset(10) - half a 22px button(11) = 319. y = window top on screen(30) + .sbnav's top inset(9) + half the button height(11) = 50, click coordinates are screen-absolute. A real OS click, so it must clear AtriumClientView::NonClientHitTest's carve before the page ever sees it.
presence only, no DOM click: a dispatched click would reload too and hide a missed OS click behind the same vlog line
